A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable versions of the same HALLUENTITY study, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices. Material from v1's Appendix B is integrated into v2's experimental sections, allowing a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses and evaluations of five uncertainty scores across 17 LLMs, including detailed results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original dataset analyses and experimental results, including the detailed comparisons consolidated into Tables 2 and 3.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, entity-level score aggregation, and five uncertainty-scoring procedures remain unchanged. Explicitly including preceding context in the CCP formula clarifies behavior already described in v1's prose.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 157 ChatGPT-generated biographies containing 18,785 entities, the same hallucination-rate scenarios, and the same RedPajama source for IDF estimation. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Likelihood, Entropy, CCP, SAR, and Focus remain the evaluated comparison methods. The focused error analyses retain the same Likelihood, SAR, and Focus comparator set.

E3.justification: The 17 LLM configurations, scoring hyperparameters, five evaluation metrics, optimal-F1 threshold procedure, and hallucination-rate groups remain unchanged. The subgroup sample counts remain 54, 59, and 44.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same model-size comparisons, hallucination-rate stratification, POS/NER and sentence-position error analyses, and three qualitative cases. Analyses moved from Appendix B into v2's main text are retained evidence, not new tests.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The same plots summarize variation across models without introducing a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 425 detailed model-by-method metric values match between v1's Tables 5–9 and v2's Tables 2–3, allowing for equivalent decimal formatting. Table 1, dataset statistics, plotted trends, and qualitative findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects the entity-span condition from i < j ≤ T to i ≤ j ≤ T, formally allowing single-token entities. This is a limited correction to the mathematical definition; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: an entity-level benchmark, evaluation across 17 LLMs, and evidence that existing uncertainty scores struggle to localize hallucinations.

C2.justification: The interpretations of SAR's weighting failures, Focus's filtering and propagation tradeoffs, and limited model-size benefits are retained. The apparently expanded POS discussion in v2 already appears in v1's Appendix B, and the stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct Hugging Face dataset link below the abstract; v1 provides only a future MIT-release statement. Hardware, computation times, hyperparameters, and annotation instructions were already disclosed in v1 and are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. Updates to the Liang et al. and Zhang et al. references identify conference versions of already cited works rather than adding new research.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. Appendix B's material is integrated into Sections 5.1–5.3 with revised transitions, the indicator function receives an explicit explanation, and the acknowledgement to ACL reviewers is removed.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column format and extensively resizes and relocates displays. Five appendix result tables become two grouped main-text tables with model identifiers. The merged Table 2 introduces an incorrect AUROC heading over the AUPRC block, although its caption names both metrics.

improvement.justification: The dataset access link and corrected single-token entity definition provide modest gains in usability and precision, while integrating Appendix B makes supporting evidence easier to locate. The empirical substance is unchanged. Table 2's new metric-header error is a localized regression, partially mitigated by its correct caption, so the overall improvement remains limited.
